title: UKPNP High Level Delegation Briefs British MPs on Kashmir Crisis and Current Situation in London House of Parliament
excerpt: A high-level UKPNP delegation led by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri briefed British MPs in the House of Parliament on the Kashmir crisis, human rights concerns, and the current political situation.
author: London Correspondent

heroImage.caption: UKPNP delegation meeting British MPs inside the UK Parliament.

body.text: A high-level delegation of the United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) met British Members of Parliament in the House of Commons to brief them on the ongoing Kashmir crisis and the deteriorating human rights situation across the region.

The delegation, led by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, included senior party members who presented a detailed briefing on the historical context of the Kashmir conflict, the current political situation, and the humanitarian challenges faced by civilians in the region.
The people of Jammu and Kashmir cannot be silenced. Their voices must be heard in the corridors of power, and their rights must be protected under international law.

During the meeting, the delegation highlighted concerns regarding political repression, arbitrary detentions, and the frequent communication blackouts that have severed contact between families and their loved ones abroad. They emphasized that such measures constitute collective punishment and violate fundamental human rights.

body.caption: Delegation members presenting documents to MPs.

body.text: The delegation also raised the issue of prolonged public protests over electricity shortages, lack of basic services, and the targeting of journalists and peaceful activists. They called for an immediate end to what they described as the militarization of civilian life.
There is no military solution to the Kashmir conflict. Only dialogue, democratic participation, and respect for human dignity can lead to a just and lasting peace.

British MPs expressed serious concern over the human rights situation and called for renewed international attention to the region. They emphasized the importance of democratic rights, freedom of expression, and the protection of civilians under international humanitarian law.

The meeting concluded with a mutual commitment to continue diplomatic engagement and to work together in raising the Kashmir issue at international forums, including the United Nations Human Rights Council and the European Parliament.

items: UKPNP delegation met with multiple British MPs across party lines
Discussions focused on human rights violations and political repression
Concerns raised over communication blackouts affecting millions
British MPs pledged to raise the issue in Parliament
Both sides agreed on the need for peaceful dialogue and international mediation
